import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers using effect size and significance
    effect_sizes = np.array([feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)].mean() for fid in feats.ids])
    t_stats = np.array([stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                       feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0] 
                       for fid in feats.ids])
    
    # Filter features with strong effect sizes and significant t-stats
    mask = (np.abs(effect_sizes) > 0.1) & (np.abs(t_stats) > 2.0)
    candidates = [fid for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids) if mask[i]]
    
    if not candidates:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Cluster correlated features to identify modules
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in candidates]].T)
    np.fill_diagonal(corr_matrix, 0)
    
    # Use hierarchical clustering to find correlated groups
    clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=2, linkage='average')
    cluster_labels = clustering.fit_predict(1 - np.abs(corr_matrix))
    
    # Select best module (largest cluster)
    module_ids = [candidates[i] for i in range(len(candidates)) if cluster_labels[i] == 0]
    if len(module_ids) < 2:
        module_ids = [candidates[i] for i in range(len(candidates)) if cluster_labels[i] == 1]
    
    if len(module_ids) < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Create weighted score from module features
    weights = np.abs(effect_sizes[[feats.column(fid) for fid in module_ids]])
    weights = weights / np.sum(weights)
    loadings = dict(zip(module_ids, weights))
    
    # Return design with module features and their loadings
    return Design(
        drivers=(module_ids[0],) if module_ids else (),
        columns=tuple(module_ids),
        products=(),
        loadings=loadings
    )
